title: U.S. House · Oregon's 5th District
area: Central Oregon (Bend, Redmond) and outer-east Portland suburbs in Clackamas County (Happy Valley, Damascus, Estacada).

context.text: Incumbent Janelle Bynum defeated Zeva Rosenbaum 82.0%-17.4% in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. Patti Adair defeated Jonathan Lockwood 59.6%-39.7% in the Republican primary; Adair also won the Libertarian ballot line. Andrea Townsend is the Pacific Green Party nominee.

summary.text: Janelle Bynum is the Democratic nominee for re-election to Oregon's 5th Congressional District, which she has represented since 2025. She previously served eight years in the Oregon House of Representatives, including as a committee chair.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from Florida A&M University and an MBA from the University of Michigan's Ross School of Business; worked as an engineer and as a McDonald's franchise owner.

Served eight years in the Oregon House of Representatives, chairing the Committee on Small Business and Economic Development and working on efforts she says added $43 billion and over 6,000 jobs to Oregon's economy.
Volunteered with the Ronald McDonald House Charities of Oregon board, Business Oregon, the Center for Women's Leadership, and the Oregon Commission on Black Affairs.

priorities.text: Says she is focused on creating good-paying jobs, strengthening public education, addressing the wildfire crisis, and lowering the cost of health care, prescription drugs and housing for working families.

positions.summary: In an April 2026 statement on tariff refunds, called the tariffs illegal and said she introduced the RELIEF Act to refund small businesses.
positions.quote: We always knew the tariffs were illegal, now it’s time to get your money back.

positions.summary: In March 2026 said she would not send more funding to ICE without major reforms, after voting against a DHS funding resolution that included ICE and CBP.
positions.quote: I’m all for funding the TSA, the Coast Guard, and FEMA, but I won’t send another dollar to ICE without major reforms.

positions.summary: In November 2025 said a funding bill failed to reverse health care cuts or extend Affordable Care Act subsidies, and that she would not vote for a deal that fails to protect health care.
positions.quote: I won’t vote for a deal that fails to protect healthcare, so I voted no.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Financial Services.

summary.text: Patti Adair is the Republican and Libertarian nominee for Oregon's 5th Congressional District. She is a sitting Deschutes County Commissioner and certified public accountant.

background.text: Born in Pendleton, Oregon, and raised on her family's ranch in Heppner; earned a degree from the University of Oregon and a CPA license from Central Washington University.

Worked as an auditor and full-cycle accountant at Moss Adams before being elected to the Deschutes County Commission in 2018 and re-elected in 2022, where she oversees more than 1,200 employees and 22 departments.
Chairs the Central Oregon Commission on Transportation and serves as the Deschutes County Fair Association liaison and on the Local Government Advisory Committee, among other boards.

priorities.text: Fiscal responsibility and oversight of tax dollars, drawing on her accounting background.
Public safety, citing her record as county commissioner on what she describes as fighting for safer communities.
Support for veterans, citing the county's veterans village program launched during her tenure as commissioner.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she testified in support of legislation allowing accessory dwelling units, which she says will increase affordable housing.
positions.quote: Testified for SB 391 in support of Accessory Dwelling Units in coordination with SB 762 which will increase affordable housing.

record.text: As Deschutes County Commissioner, has overseen the county's veterans village program and chairs the Central Oregon Commission on Transportation.

candidates.name: Andrea Townsend

summary.text: Andrea Townsend is the Pacific Green Party nominee for Oregon's 5th Congressional District; she was also the Pacific Green nominee for the seat in 2024.
